The game

Simple rules. Big maps. No hiding spot is safe for long.

Pass the tag

One player is IT. Everyone else runs.

Only IT can tag. Catch someone and they become IT. Every second you stay clear of IT is a point, and the highest score when time runs out wins.

Freeze after a tag
1.5 s
No tag-backs for
3.5 s
Round length
60 to 120 s

Three maps

A school, a city, and the arena where it started.

School is 150 metres of classrooms, halls, a gym and a sports field. City is 250 metres of streets, alleys and towers. The Arena is small and frantic. Online, the lobby votes on where to play.

See the maps

Practice

Up to fourteen tigers, and they tag each other too.

Practice drops you into a timed round with a pack of tiger bots. They chase around walls and through doors, and they pass the tag between themselves, so any of them can end up IT.

Grab the glowing speed gems for a burst of pace, and dash to slip past a tiger at the last second.

How a round plays

Four things to know

  1. Pick a map. Choose under Practice map, or vote with everyone in an online lobby.
  2. Find the red ball. It floats over whoever is IT. Above you, chase. Above anyone else, run.
  3. Pass the tag. IT touches another player and they take over. They freeze for a moment, so use the head start.
  4. Stay safe. Every second you are not IT is a point. Getting tagged never ends your round.

Move your mouse or finger over the field to control the teal player.

Modes

Play alone or with friends

Practice

You against 6, 10 or 14 tigers depending on the map. Touch a tiger while you are IT to pass it on. Your safe time goes on the leaderboard.

Multiplayer

Join the public game, which starts by itself, or make a private room and share its four-letter code. Bots fill in when there aren't many people. Everyone gets their own colour and a win count.

News

Patch notes

November 2026

Multiplayer bots

  • Bots join online games when there aren't many people, so you never wait alone.
  • Three settings: Off, Auto (the default, fills a room up to 4 players) and On (fills up to 6).
  • The host of a private room picks the setting in the lobby. The public game always uses Auto.
  • Bots chase, run, dash and pass the tag just like players, and find their way around the School and City.
November 2026

Game feel

  • 3-2-1-GO countdown, beeps for the last 10 seconds and a final buzzer.
  • Sound effects for tags, being IT, dashing, pickups and footsteps.
  • Dash: a quick burst of speed every 2.5 seconds. The tigers dash too.
  • Speed gems on every map: 5 seconds of extra speed and unlimited sprint.
  • Minimap on School and City, plus sprint and dash bars.
  • Shadows, distance fog, richer colours and a camera that kicks when you sprint.
November 2026

Spectate

  • Watch any public game or Practice round live, in 3D in the game or from above on this site.
  • Follow any player, or fly around with a free camera.
  • Allow spectators switch for Practice and Multiplayer, on unless you turn it off.
  • The game now plays right on this website.
October 2026

The big update

  • School and City maps, with map voting online and a map picker for Practice.
  • Pass-the-tag: one IT at a time, scored in seconds spent safe.
  • Practice is a timed round with 6 to 14 tigers that tag each other.
  • A banner pops up for every tag. Orbit camera for mouse, touch and controller.

FAQ

Questions

How many people can play together?

Up to eight players share a room.

What is the red ball?

It floats over whoever is IT. If it is above you, chase someone. If it is above someone else, run.

Why does Multiplayer take so long to connect?

The game server sleeps when nobody is using it. The first player to connect wakes it up, which can take up to a minute.

Can I play on a phone or with a controller?

Yes. Phones get an on-screen joystick and sprint button, and a controller works with the left stick for moving and the right stick for the camera.

What are the bots in Multiplayer?

Computer players that join when a room is quiet. The host of a private room can set them to Off, Auto (fill up to 4 players) or On (fill up to 6). The public game uses Auto, so you can start playing even when nobody else is online.

Can people watch me play?

Yes, while Allow spectators is on. Turn it off on the title screen for Practice, or in the Multiplayer menu, and you disappear from the Watch list and from other people's views.

Does getting tagged end my round?

No. Every round runs the full time. Being IT only stops your safe seconds from counting.
